findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment: Observed boxes of single service. Articles to be stored on the floor of the dry storage room. They were received yesterday. They are being moved up onto storage racks now. 4-903.11: (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Chicken strips and rib meats in the hot pass through for lunch service are 116°F and 119°F respectively. Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was rapidly reheated to above 165°F . Reference 3-501.16(A)(1). Some food was served with the control being time and knowledge that food was in the hot holding pass through for approximately 2 hours. Watch unit and keep closed

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment: 4-204-112  (C) A thermometer is not provided in the hot pass through. Provide independant thermometer to validate unit temperatuer. Cold/Hot holding equipment used for Time/Temperature Control for Safety food shall have at least one thermometer in an easily viewed location. Reference 4-204-112.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Clean Equipment/Utensils/Linens/Single-Use Articles stored incorrectly with handles in the food. Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D). Find proper method to store tongs so that they are not going into the food.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

Eliminate live pests using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111. Spot checks will continue until all that is obersed are dead roaches. There needs to be a plan developed to eliminate the pests from the facility. The live roach fell from the door to the mechanical room when it was opened. It appears that there is a live roach up by the speaker by the dish machine. The premises shall be maintained free of insects, rodents and other pests. Eliminate roaches using proper pest control processes as needed. Reference 6-501.111. Continue to aggressively treat the roach problem. Submit plan in  writing to SCDPH.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: Observed a serving spoon with food debris on it to be hanging with the other clean spoons. 750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be properly washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use and any time they may have become contaminated.  The spoon (and one behind it) was removed and put through the dish machine.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

Clean and maintain clean. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.comment: Observed measureing cups to be stored in the drawer of the prep table. The containers holding these cups are soled. Wash rinse and sanitize the cups and containers. 750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Hood vent in the facility is not clean and has some grease running down the wall. This grease could provide a food source for pests and hood vent shall be maintained free of accumulated grease and soil. 750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Observed some issues in the facility that can contribute to roach harborage. There are holes in the walls in the dry storage both in the back corner under the window and in the wall and at the lines that are attached to the water heater for the kitchen. Also, there is a wooden pass through window which is no longer used and has openings up into the ceiling and walls which would allow roaches to come straight into the facility kitchen unhindered. Suggest removing pass through as it is not used and has not been used for more than 5 years according to facility staff. Provide smooth cleansable surface where window is currently located.  750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text:
750.160 & 280 - Employee was observed having bare hand contact with sandwiches as they were being placed in plastic bags. Proper handwashing and glove use when handling ready to eat foods were discussed with the employee and manager. Employee bagging sandwiches washed his hands and put on a pair of gloves before continuing with food handling.

Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. When handling ready to eat foods suitable utensils (i.e. gloves, tongs, spoons, deli tissue) must be used to minimize bare hand contact.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Baking sheets were observed being wiped down with sanitizer solution and set aside to dry at the 3 part sink as the final step of ware washing process. Manager was advised that baking sheets need to be submerged in the sanitizer for 60 seconds prior to being set aside to air dry. One half needs to be submerged for 60 seconds, and then flipped and the other half needs to be submerged for 60 seconds prior to setting aside to air dry. The baking sheets just went through wash and rinse steps and were sanitized properly after discussing the process with the manager.

Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4).

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text:
750.860 - Pan holding clean serving utensils was soiled with food splash/crumbs. Maintain storage areas clean to protect utensils and equipment from potential contamination.
 
Cleaned and sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - Kitchen handsink was soiled with grimy buildup/splash in the basin and along the top surfaces (around faucet, etc.). Clean handsinks and all related fixtures as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Handsinks and all fixtures shall be maintained clean and in good repair.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee handled personal phone and went back to 3 part sink to continue with ware washing and did not wash hands. Proper handwashing and when to wash hands were discussed. 

Hands must be properly washed between tasks, prior to putting on gloves, between glove changes, and before handling food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles. Keep in mind personal items, such as cell phones, clothing, etc., are not considered clean surfaces. If you have to adjust clothing, use the phone, or do any tasks unrelated to food prep that involve touching general surfaces then hands must immediately be washed prior to returning to food prep/service, ware washing, or any other tasks (i.e. putting away clean dishes, handling unwrapped single service articles, etc.)
Proper handwashing technique must be used every time. When shutting off the manual faucet use a paper towel after hands have been dried or use an elbow, etc. to avoid recontamination of freshly washed hands.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Two carts with trays of pizza slices were observed next to the range-top oven . Pizza slices were observed to have surface temperatures of 54F-68F. Employee stated the pizza slices were pulled from the freezer and placed on trays around 7:30-7:45a. Four trays of pizza slices were immediately placed in the oven to begin baking. Remaining trays were temporarily placed in the freezer for cold holding until room was available in the oven to bake more slices.
Cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) must be maintained at proper cold holding temperature of 41F/below until they are ready for steps involving preparation. Once prep is complete, cold PHF must be placed immediately in the oven if cooking is required. If foods will be cooked but are not ready to be placed in the oven then store PHF in coolers or immediately back in the freezer (for frozen pizza, etc.) until they are ready for use. Do not store PHF at ambient temperature for any length of time. Limit the amount of time PHF spends in the temperature danger zone.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - Sweet potatoes being portioned for hot holding had surface temperatures ranging from 94F (potatoes still left in pan) to 120F (potatoes already portioned but not yet in the warmer). Employee responsible for cooking canned sweet potatoes was asked about prep/hot holding. Sweet potatoes were pulled from the convection oven around 8:30a and placed on top of the oven for ~30 minutes prior to being portioned to be placed in warmer before service. Employee did not verify a cooking temperature to know how hot the potatoes were prior to being portioned. All portions of sweet potatoes were reheated in the steamer prior to being placed back in the warmer. 
All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 135F/above after being properly cooked/reheated. Hold hot PHF at 135F/above until foods are ready to be portioned. Immediately place cooked/reheated foods in the warmer for hot holding until further prep is ready to occur.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Quat test strips were observed to have signs of water damage (discolored/did not register a color comparable to ppm chart when used). All damaged test strips were discarded. The chart was legible and kept for use. Inspector left a few test strips for the staff to use the remainder of the operating day. Manager called to order a new set of test strips during the inspection.  
A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text:
750.820 - Sanitizer concentration in 3 part sink was at 100ppm quat. Also, a pan going through manual ware washing was washed, rinsed, and briefly dunked into sanitizer solution prior to being placed on drain board to air dry. Employees were advised to sanitize all food contact surfaces for 1 minute after being washed/rinsed and prior to being placed on the drain board to air dry. Sanitizer solution was remade to be at proper concentration of 200ppm.
Equipment and utensils shall be sanitized in the third compartment according to one of the methods included in section 750.820 (e) (1) through (4). Maintain Steramine solutions at 200ppm quat. Use test strips to verify concentrations are correct.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - String cheese in chest freezer had internal temperature of 63F. Freezer was not holding temp (see #4). Box of Land of Lakes string cheese (168 sticks) was discarded in the trash. Cold PHF must be maintained at proper temperature of 41/below in coolers and maintained frozen in freezers. Maintain cold PHF at proper temperatures. Use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to monitor temperatures of foods during prep, cooking, storage, and service.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Hotdogs had internal temperature of 118F. Burner holding pot on the stove was off. Burner was lit and hotdogs were reheated to 193F. Another pot of hotdogs on the stove were held at temps well above 135F (burner for other pot was on low). Hot PHF must be maintained at 135F/above after foods have been cooked/reheated to proper temperatures. Maintain hot PHF at proper temperatures. Use clean, calibrated stem thermometers to monitor temperatures of foods during prep, cooking, storage, and service.

findings.title: Facilities to maintain proper temperatures
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Chest freezer in storage room was at 58F according to inspector's stem thermometer. Hanging thermometer in the bottom of the freezer was broken and could not be used for temperature comparison. String cheese was discarded (see #3a). Bags of shredded cheese, packaged turkey ham, and garlic bread slices were thawed and/or thawing and were still at temperatures between 29F and 40F. The aforementioned products were moved to a cooler holding at proper temp or used for service today dependent upon needs of kitchen staff. Kitchen manager unplugged the freezer and took it our of service. Freezers shall be able to maintain frozen foods frozen.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text: 750.140 - Thermometer in chest freezer was broken. Thermometer was removed from freezer to be discarded. Cold holding units used to hold PHF shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F. Maintain functioning thermometers in all coolers and freezers to monitor temperatures within units and ensure they are able to maintain PHF at proper temperatures.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text: 750.690 - Wooden dish rack storage shelf below sprayer sink was worn along the edge where paint has come off. Bare wood was present. Re-paint the shelf to provide a smooth, easily cleanable surface. Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - A) Ledge below far left end of dish counter wall to the left of the sprayer sink was soiled with debris. Clean off the ledge. B) Hood over dish machine was soiled with dust accumulation. Clean the hood and minimize the amount of dust inside the exhaust pipe. Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1280 - Personal belongings (coats/purses) were observed hanging on dry storage shelves around food and on top of the chest freezer in the dry storage room. A personal cell phone was observed on outer cover of plastic wrap box. Storage of personal belongings was discussed with Kitchen Manager and staff. Designate a separate area for personal storage. An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation/storage areas and away from all food related items (i.e. single service articles and clean equipment/utensils) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 - Employees were observed having bare hand contact with ready to eat foods (see #12 A). Employees put on gloves to finish food prep. Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact. When handling ready to eat foods use suitable utensils (gloves, tongs, scoop, deli tissue, etc.)

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text: 750.160 & 512 - (x2) A) Employees were observed handling cooked hotdogs and buns without wearing gloves. When asked to put on gloves employees did so without first washing their hands. Hands must be washed before putting on gloves, between glove changes, and as needed when hands may have become contaminated. B) Employee was observed wearing the same pair of gloves for more than one task - went from food prep, to touching soiled utensil storage container/setting up 3 part sink for ware washing, and went back to food prep. Employee was advised on proper glove use and washing hands prior to putting on a new pair of gloves. Gloves are meant to be used for only one task and must be changed between tasks or when they become soiled or torn. **Educational materials on when to wash hands and proper use of gloves were provided**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) large black floor fan (dust buildup - not being used at time of inspection); B) lower shelf of kitchen prep table (crumbs); & C) storage cabinets of food line counter (crumbs/debris). Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - Clean scoops were observed in storage containers with food surfaces extended up in dry storage room. Cleaned and sanitized utensils and equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means. Store clean utensils with handles extended up out of containers to avoid touching clean food contact surfaces when retrieving utensils.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: Observed ceiling tile missing from the area above the door of the dry storage. Section 750.1210 Replace the ceiling tile.
